Clearly (1) implies (2) and (2) implies (3) by restricting to
more divisible degrees and powers of invertible sheaves.
Also (3) implies (4) by the uniqueness statement
in Lemma <REF_0001>.
Thus we have to prove that (4) implies (1). Assume (4),
in other words <MATH_0001>.
Note that this implies that we may write
<MATH_0002> and
<MATH_0003>.
Moreover, via these identifications we have that the graded ring
maps <MATH_0004> and <MATH_0005> correspond to the restriction of the canonical
graded ring map
<MATH_0006>
to <MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008> composed with pullback by <MATH_0009>
(by Lemma <REF_0002> again). Hence taking
<MATH_0010> to be the isomorphism
<MATH_0011>
works.
